tasks.short: Choose publication colours, produce separations, and check that they meet the print specification.

steps.what: Read the publication brief and printer specification in {EMAIL}.
Inspect artwork inks and colour spaces in the {OTHER} prepress application.
Choose process and spot colours in the {OTHER} prepress application.
Generate separation files using the {OTHER} prepress application.
Review separation proofs in {DOCS} and approve the files.

tasks.design: Configure printer presets and separation checks in the {OTHER} prepress application, using approved specifications held in {DOCS}. A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} supplies print requirements; the desktop publisher chooses the colour plan and approves separation proofs before downstream release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printer specifications arrived separately from artwork. Presets varied, and colour choices involved brand appearance, substrate and print cost.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing prepress controls already handle ink inventories and separations. Faster implementation makes specification intake, preset maintenance and linked proofs cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: Screens cannot fully predict ink on a particular substrate. Special finishes, overprints and unusual spot colours still need experienced judgement or a physical proof.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the printed result preserves the intended appearance within the available budget.

ambition.what: Per-edition comparison of process-only and spot-colour options

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated separation setup toward evaluating difficult colour choices. Existing colour approval and spending authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare artwork that reproduces consistently across print substrates.
reach.learn: Colour management, ink limits, overprint behaviour and physical proof evaluation.

evidence.claim: Prepress applications commonly provide ink inventories, separation previews and reusable output presets.
Substrate effects and special inks can require physical proofs despite automated technical checks.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured case results.

assumptions: Most jobs use an established printer and known print specifications.
Structured intake replaces routine reading of specification emails; unusual requirements enter an exception queue.
The {OTHER} prepress application supports presets and separation inspection.
Access estimates include assessing employee consultation under national rules; required consultation may extend the range.
GDPR applies where artwork contains personal data. Applicable EU AI Act obligations must be assessed if model features are introduced.
unknowns: Which prepress application and automation interfaces are available?
How many jobs use special inks, finishes or unfamiliar substrates?
Who approves colour choices and additional print spending?
Are printer specifications current and reusable?
Which national consultation requirements apply to this workplace?
research_questions: Which configured checks detect unintended spot inks and overprints in the supported file formats?
Which proofing method provides sufficient confidence for each substrate and finish?
new_work: Maintain printer presets and specification versions.
Investigate unexpected inks and failed separation checks.
Review generated proofs and request physical proofs where needed.
Revalidate presets when a printer changes its process.

tasks.short: Convert publication files into print or web formats, check the result, and deliver the correct version.

steps.what: Read destination and delivery requirements in {EMAIL}.
Choose export settings in the {OTHER} conversion application.
Export publication files in the {OTHER} conversion application.
Inspect converted pages and preflight results in the {OTHER} validation application.
Approve delivery and send publication files through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} selects approved export profiles in the {OTHER} conversion application and stores versioned outputs and preflight reports in {DOCS}. A small integration prepares delivery through {EMAIL} or upload to {CMS}; the desktop publisher checks the output and approves the destination-specific release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Destination requirements, source versions and export settings were disconnected. Unusual fonts, effects and legacy formats made unattended conversion unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export presets and preflight tools handle standard formats. Faster coding makes version tracking, delivery preparation and exception routing economical.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy files, missing fonts and flattened content can lose fidelity. Accessible web documents may require manual reading-order and semantic checks.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a technically valid conversion that changes meaning, readability or visual emphasis.

ambition.what: Versioned print-and-web release pack with a linked preflight report

tasks.altitude: Routine export setup and file delivery occupy less of the week. The desktop publisher can offer a traceable release pack; publication approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Specify publication assets for accessible, responsive web use.
reach.learn: Web image formats, compression, document accessibility and responsive asset requirements.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting repeatable publication generation.
The template evidence does not establish reliable conversion of arbitrary legacy files.
Export profiles and preflight checks can automate standard conversions, with human review for fidelity and accessibility.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The {OTHER} conversion application supports reusable profiles and batch export.
Print requirements apply to print outputs; web requirements apply to web outputs.
Future routine requests use structured destination fields instead of free-text email instructions.
File delivery and upload are gated; direct website publication requires the existing publication approval.
Access estimates include assessing consultation under national rules; required consultation may extend the range.
GDPR applies to personal data in source and output files. Any introduced model use also needs assessment under the EU AI Act.
unknowns: Which source and destination formats account for most jobs?
Can the installed conversion tools run unattended under current licences?
What accessibility requirements apply to the outputs?
Does delivery mean printer handoff, draft upload or direct publication?
Who may approve each destination and release?
research_questions: Which format pairs preserve fonts, transparency, links and reading order reliably?
Which preflight checks and visual comparisons expose meaningful conversion failures?
How should retries prevent duplicate delivery or release of an outdated version?
new_work: Maintain destination profiles and regression samples.
Resolve missing fonts and unsupported source formats.
Review flagged visual changes and accessibility issues.
Approve releases and investigate failed deliveries.
Maintain version links and destination credentials.

tasks.short: Capture source material, enter digitized content, and import checked assets into a prepress project.

steps.what: Download supplied assets from {EMAIL} and place working copies in {DOCS}.
Digitize physical originals using the {OTHER} scanner or camera capture application.
Transcribe required text and tables in the {OTHER} prepress application.

loop.input: Scanned text and tables lacking usable embedded text.
loop.output: Draft digitized copy linked to source regions.
loop.check: Check page coverage and table dimensions; show source overlays for human checking of wording, names and numbers.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per page, within a configured page limit; unreadable content returns to manual transcription.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use embedded text or configured OCR first. A bounded model handles only irregular layouts and ambiguous residual text.

steps.what: Import content and link assets in the {OTHER} prepress application.
Check imported content and approve the project in the {OTHER} prepress application.

tasks.design: Have contributors supply source assets directly to a controlled folder in {DOCS}, removing the desktop publisher's download-and-copy step. A deterministic importer links assets to the {OTHER} prepress application, with configured capture and OCR plus a bounded extraction loop for difficult residual text; source-linked checks precede project approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material arrived through different channels with inconsistent names and formats. Physical originals, weak scans and fragile import interfaces still required hands-on work.
tasks.enabler_now: Direct file intake and import scripts remove repeated handling. Existing OCR and small source-linked extraction loops can reduce transcription without assuming perfect recognition.
tasks.still_hard: Someone must handle physical originals. Poor scans, handwriting, complex tables and absent asset rights still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when captured material is incomplete, misleading or unsuitable for publication.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to copying files, typing and relinking assets; more goes to source quality and exceptions. Approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare structured source content and reusable publication assets.
reach.learn: Content structure, asset metadata, table semantics and source traceability.

evidence.claim: Direct digital intake and scripted asset linking can remove repeated file handling.
OCR and bounded extraction can reduce transcription, but difficult publication content still requires source comparison.
The digest provides no documented publication-prepress case establishing these savings.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Digital submissions dominate; physical capture is an occasional part of the workload.
The shares describe the average mix of jobs, not a requirement to scan every job.
Contributors can submit directly to {DOCS}; this shifts a small amount of intake responsibility to them.
Usable embedded text bypasses extraction, and imported content remains a draft until project approval.
The {OTHER} prepress application exposes an import interface or supported scripting mechanism.
GDPR applies to personal data in originals and extracted copy; processing access and retention need controls.
Applicable EU AI Act duties and consultation under national rules need assessment; required consultation may extend the access range.
unknowns: What proportion of material arrives on paper, as images or as usable digital text?
Which source languages and table types are common?
Can contributors submit directly to the document store?
Which import and asset-linking interfaces are available?
May source material be processed by an external model service?
Who confirms image rights and source completeness?
research_questions: How accurately does configured OCR handle representative scans before a model is added?
Which source-linked checks catch omitted text, changed numbers and broken table structure?
Can imports be retried without duplicating content or breaking links?
new_work: Teach contributors the intake format and required metadata.
Review extracted copy against source regions.
Handle unreadable originals and missing assets.
Maintain import mappings, folder permissions and extraction limits.
Check extraction quality when source types or models change.

tasks.short: Edit publication images through masking, pixel corrections and retouching, then approve and export the result.

steps.what: Read edit instructions in {EMAIL} and retrieve source assets from {DOCS}.
Inspect images and choose corrections in the {OTHER} image editing application.
Mask, correct and retouch images in the {OTHER} image editing application.

loop.input: Source image, explicit edit plan and protected image regions.
loop.output: Reversible masks or local cleanup proposals in an edit draft.
loop.check: Compare with the source; verify dimensions and protected regions; inspect edges, texture, product accuracy and unintended changes.
loop.stop: One proposal and one revision per asset within a configured asset limit; failed or ambiguous edits return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use configured actions for resizing and fixed corrections. Irregular boundaries and local textures can need a model proposal followed by human refinement.

steps.what: Review the edit draft in {DOCS} and approve its appearance.
Export approved assets from the {OTHER} image editing application into {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Structured requests in {WORKFLOW} link source assets and brand guidance from {DOCS} to the {OTHER} image editing application. Configured actions handle routine corrections and exports, while a bounded model proposes reversible masks or cleanup; the desktop publisher refines the edits and the graphic designer approves their use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Retouching combines irregular image content with subjective visual choices. Repeated requests lacked clear instructions, protected regions and reusable export settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing editing actions cover predictable operations. Faster integration work and bounded model proposals can reduce masking effort while preserving source comparison and manual refinement.
tasks.still_hard: Hair, transparent objects, reflections and detailed textures remain difficult. Edits can subtly misrepresent people or products even when they look convincing.
tasks.human_edge: Choose restrained corrections that preserve visual credibility, product truth and the intended tone.

ambition.what: Crop comparison across campaign formats before final image approval

tasks.altitude: The desktop publisher spends less time on routine setup and initial masks, and more on difficult edges and visual choices. Image approval remains with the graphic designer; no new publication authority is assumed.

reach.task: Develop image direction and crops for a campaign.
reach.learn: Composition, art direction, colour consistency and truthful image treatment.

evidence.claim: Configured image-editing actions can automate repeated sizing, corrections and exports.
Model-assisted masks and cleanup can reduce initial editing effort but need close inspection and manual refinement.
The digest contains no documented image-retouching case supporting a measured saving for this task.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Routine requests can move to structured intake; ambiguous briefs still require clarification.
A graphic designer reviews publication imagery; another designated reviewer may hold this role locally.
Source images are retained, and edits remain reversible.
The editing application supports actions and a usable model-assisted editing interface.
Model use is limited to approved masking and cleanup operations rather than unrestricted image replacement.
GDPR applies to identifiable people in images; applicable EU AI Act duties depend on the actual editing use.
Access estimates include assessing employee consultation under national rules; required consultation may extend the range.
unknowns: Which editing application and model-assisted features are licensed?
How much editing is routine correction versus detailed creative retouching?
Which regions or image characteristics must never change?
Who approves image edits and confirms usage rights?
Can identifiable images leave the controlled environment?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed change?
research_questions: Do bounded proposals preserve product details, text and protected regions on representative images?
Which edits are reliably handled by existing configured actions?
What quality threshold makes a model proposal faster than manual editing after review?
new_work: Specify permitted edits and protected image regions.
Inspect model proposals and repair difficult masks.
Maintain editing actions, export profiles and source comparisons.
Review changes in model behaviour against representative images.
Keep approval records and resolve unclear image rights.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward visual quality, difficult source material and release readiness as repeated intake, setup and export work shrinks. The role can coordinate a traceable publication pack, while existing creative, budget and publication approval rights remain in place.
reach: Graphic design: prepare consistent colour reproduction, image treatments and campaign crops.
Web and digital interface design: specify usable publication assets and check accessible outputs.
Technical writing: improve source structure, table semantics and asset traceability.
skills_to_grow: Prepress presets, colour management and proof evaluation.
Structured content intake and asset metadata.
Export automation, preflight checks and version control.
Source-linked OCR review and exception handling.
Image comparison, reversible editing and model evaluation.
Accessible document and web asset preparation.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a publication readiness service that turns approved source packs into traceable print and web outputs, with clear technical checks and targeted human visual approval.
